rationale: Greek loanword καιρός 'appointed/decisive moment' (distinct from χρόνος = duration). Recurs throughout this page (lines 6, 9, 12, 15, 18) as the specific time of cosmic events. Distinguished from ⲡⲥⲏⲩ 'the time' which appears in parallel construction.
Lycopolitan reflex of Coptic ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, delay.' Used in line 17 of the Five Gods being established/tarrying within the First Man for a long time before being summoned forth.
Coptic verb 'reach, arrive at.' Used in line 23 of the Mother of Life reaching the earth at the end of myriads of years — cosmological-temporal arrival verb.
Likely related to Sahidic ⲣⲡⲣⲡ̄ 'twinkle, flash.' In line 33 with ⲛ̄-ⲃⲉⲗ 'of an eye' — the biblical 'twinkling of an eye' (1 Cor 15:52) idiom for instantaneous moment.

proposed_english: the three that belong / the three reckoned
rationale: ⲡϣⲁⲙⲧ = 'the three' (Lyc. ϣⲟⲙⲧ̄), ⲉⲧⲏⲡ qualitative of ⲱⲡ 'count, belong, be reckoned to.' In line 26: 'one of the three reckoned to the place of the Twelve Aeons' — likely a triadic subdivision within the Twelve.
